segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 10th, 2026.
Today we cover breakthroughs in agentic systems, new NVIDIA hardware, and massive AI models for robotics.
Tune in for the latest updates.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Can Agentic Robotics Solve Robotics’ Data-Scaling Problem?".
This story explores how artificial intelligence agents can utilize simulation to solve complex robotics problems by relying on code rather than solely on large datasets.
An example demonstrated an agentic robotic arm successfully depositing used hypodermic needles into a disposal box by navigating variable subchallenges, such as different box shapes.

Agentic systems leverage simulation to enable agents to learn and execute complex physical tasks, suggesting a potential method for addressing the data-scaling problem in robotics through this new paradigm.
This approach indicates a pathway for overcoming data limitations in the field of robotics.
The development points toward increased capability for autonomous physical task execution in complex environments.
From The Robot Report, NVIDIA launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL.
This report details the introduction of the updated open frontier world action model GR00T 2 and the latest open-source robot learning framework Isaac Lab 3.0 at the CoRL conference.
GR00T 2 facilitates the learning of dexterous manipulation skills from diverse data and enables skill transfer between different robotic bodies.
Isaac Lab 3.0, integrated with Newton, supports efficient and parallel simulation training for complex robotic systems using accurate physics.
New evaluation benchmarks such as DexBench and VABAR are currently emerging to quantify robot dexterity across industrial applications.
These advancements are being utilized by various partners in robotics research and industrial deployment.
The developments signal progression in enabling more capable and adaptable robotic systems for practical tasks.
From Robotics & Automation News, Nature Will launches 50-billion-parameter AI model for dexterous robot hands.

This report details the launch of Natura-1, a physical general foundation model designed for dexterous hand control, demonstrating the capacity to combine instruction following with the ability to manipulate objects under varying circumstances.
The model was pre-trained on over a million hours of egocentric human data to learn the complex relationship between human intent and physical action.
This achievement was accomplished through multimodal training involving language, images, video, and physical actions.
Natura-1 operates with a one hundred-millisecond control loop to unify language, vision, and high-degree-of-freedom action.
This work establishes a progression toward general foundation models capable of effective real-world physical interaction.
This development signals a significant advance in enabling robots to interact with the physical world through sophisticated learned control.
From Robotics & Automation News, GenRobot AI raises one hundred million dollars in a Series A plus funding round to expand its robot training data infrastructure.

The company focuses on the equipment and software required to capture, process, and organize human demonstrations for robot training, addressing the challenge of obtaining sufficient high-quality data for teaching robots complex physical tasks.
GenRobot AI provides recording systems and a software platform named Matrix designed to prepare raw data for machine learning.
This investment reflects increasing investor interest in the foundational data infrastructure supporting embodied artificial intelligence development.
The development indicates a growing focus on the necessary systems for training embodied artificial intelligence systems.
Future developments in robot training data processing are anticipated.
From NVIDIA Blog, "Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation".
This report details methods developed by NVIDIA and partners at CoRL for training robots to perform delicate manipulation tasks through simulation.
The demonstration utilized world action models such as GR00T 2 to enable robots to learn dexterous skills by utilizing diverse data and skill transfer.
The Isaac Lab framework was employed, integrating accurate physics to facilitate scalable training within simulation environments using agents and tools like Newton.
Agentic robotics approaches, including the Graph-as-Policy framework, were used to coordinate multiple skills into complex robot programs, supported by benchmarks such as DexBench.
These advancements seek to connect simulation training with real-world industrial deployment.
The progress indicates a pathway toward more effective and scalable training for complex robotic systems.
From Boston Dynamics Blog, "Atlas On a Roll".

This report details an experiment where a controls engineer tested the limits of the Atlas robot's actuators by retrofitting wheels onto the robot's feet, demonstrating the synergistic relationship between low-level motor control and high-level reinforcement learning.
The experiment involved creating motion trajectories based on human data and training a reinforcement learning policy to manage the rolling motion.

This process pushed the motors to their performance envelopes, emphasizing the necessity of closing the simulation-to-real gap by ensuring simulated motor behavior accurately reflected the physical hardware.
The work ultimately demonstrated the critical interplay between precise motor control and advanced learning algorithms in robotics.
This research highlights ongoing efforts to bridge simulation accuracy with physical reality in advanced robotic systems.
From The Robot Report, Boston Dynamics adds wheels to Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control.

This story details an experiment where wheels were attached to the Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control by merging physics-based motor control with reinforcement learning, demonstrating improved dynamic stability across unstructured terrain.
The experiment involved a simple retrofit of an off-the-shelf scooter rim onto the ankle actuator to allow Atlas to process real-time feedback.
Atlas successfully demonstrated the ability to switch smoothly between rolling on flat surfaces and articulated legged motion over obstacles.
This research emphasizes that combining classical control with whole-body reinforcement learning yields superior real-world agility.
This advancement suggests a pathway toward more capable and adaptable robotic systems in complex physical environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, Rogue Cortex emerges from stealth with $4.5 million to simplify robotics development.
This report details the recent funding secured by the UK robotics startup to facilitate the simplification of robotic system development through specialized software and hardware tools.

The company introduced a hardware-agnostic Software Development Kit enabling development without hardware constraints, alongside the Drone Developer Kit, a configurable drone platform integrated with avionics.
This methodology allows developers to concentrate on application creation rather than the complexities of hardware integration, with tools being provided via a per-system licensing model.
This strategic move aims to lower the barrier to entry for robotics engineering.
The development indicates a shift toward software-centric approaches in robotics creation.
From Robotics & Automation News, ANYbotics begins deliveries of ANYmal X robot for hazardous industrial environments.
This report details the commencement of deliveries for the ANYmal X quadruped robot, a legged inspection system designed for autonomous examination of assets in hazardous industrial settings.
The robot utilizes thermal cameras, acoustic sensors, and gas detectors to autonomously identify potential issues within facilities such as oil, gas, and chemical plants.
The system is engineered to comply with ATEX and IECEx explosion-protection standards through features including nitrogen-filled enclosures and flameproof protection for all components.
Furthermore, the ANYmal X operates with Shift software enabling direct integration of inspection data with industrial maintenance systems like SAP.
Early deployments include Equinor and DSM-Firmenich, with testing participation from major energy corporations including BP and Shell.
This development signals a progression in deploying autonomous sensing technology within highly regulated industrial sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: Supervised autonomy in robotics starts with the robot’s worst day".
This segment discusses the necessity of designing supervised autonomy by focusing on handling unforeseen situations rather than just smooth operation.

The methodology involves inventorizing exceptions where autonomy fails, with some exceptions resolved autonomously and others mandating human intervention, particularly concerning safety or customer rules.
Requests for assistance require providing context, confidence estimates, and time constraints to effectively engage supervisors.
A clear supervisor role must be established to balance robot autonomy with human oversight through data-driven ratios and the development of new skills.
Documenting these operational limits serves to protect commercial interests and addresses trust concerns in autonomous systems.
This work indicates a shift toward robust safety protocols in autonomous systems.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Make a Robot Arm Feel Weightless with NVIDIA Holoscan 5".
This report details how NVIDIA Holoscan 5 enables low-latency robotic control and high-throughput perception through a unified programming model for CPU and GPU workloads.
A gravity-compensation loop was demonstrated using three custom Holoscan operators to calculate inverse dynamics with Pinocchio and command a reBot arm.
The framework utilizes execution partitions and drop-oldest queues to minimize latency and jitter within the control path.
Profiling with Nsight Systems indicated that pinning the control partition significantly reduced the p99.99 latency for both C++ and Python implementations.
This methodology establishes a foundation for constructing more intricate systems such as hand-guided teaching and manipulation.
This development points toward advancements in real-time physical simulation and complex robotic interaction systems.
From Humanoids Daily, "MACHINA Summit Moves to the Palais des Congrès for 2027, Names Wandercraft, Agility and Skild AI Speakers".
This report details the venue and confirmed speakers for the upcoming MACHINA Summit.
The event is scheduled for July 7th and 8th, 2027, at the Palais des Congrès in Paris and is anticipated to host three thousand five hundred attendees and two hundred speakers.
Confirmed participants include Matthieu Masselin, CEO of Wandercraft, Jonathan Hurst, co-founder of Agility Robotics, and Abhinav Gupta, co-founder of Skild AI.
The summit is designed to establish a central European location for the physical artificial intelligence industry, incorporating a closing gala and the MACHINA Factory.
This event signals a focused effort toward consolidating the physical AI sector within Europe.
From Robotics & Automation News, Cyngn launches subscription service for autonomous material handling.

This story details the introduction of DriveMod EasyLaunch, a subscription service designed to facilitate the deployment of autonomous material handling for manufacturers and warehouses by automating repetitive material movement routes.

The program allows qualifying customers to utilize Cyngn's autonomous tuggers on a monthly basis, requiring no upfront capital and enabling deployment within weeks by removing implementation friction.
The service focuses specifically on the indoor movement of items such as carts and pallets between different operational areas.
Cyngn manages the deployment and configuration of the vehicles, and customers monitor all activity through the Cyngn Insight software.
This development signals a shift toward accessible, friction-reduced automation solutions for industrial logistics.
Future developments in the field will focus on scaling these subscription models across various operational environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, Berkshire Grey unveils enhanced AI capabilities powered by BG Pilot software.
This report details new artificial intelligence enhancements introduced for the company's robotic automation portfolio, achieving greater reliability in managing complex warehouse workflows.
The upgrades encompass advanced perception for trailer unloading, intelligent orchestration for store replenishment, and AI-driven precision packing.
The BG Pilot software utilizes insights derived from extensive real-world warehouse operations to manage variability effectively.
Specific product features are powered by dedicated modules: Scoop for perception, Stride for orchestration, and Core for packing.
This innovation allows robots to handle complex, changing warehouse workflows with increased reliability.
The development indicates a push toward more adaptable and robust automation solutions in the logistics sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, "From TractEasy to TLD Robotics: A new chapter in autonomous airport operations".

This report details the formation of TLD Robotics through the consolidation of expertise from EasyMile, TractEasy, and TLD's existing vehicle activities, which integrates technology, manufacturing, and operational experience accumulated since 2017.

The newly formed entity aims to simplify the integration of autonomous driving, vehicle manufacturing, and fleet management for ground operations by offering a complete system encompassing both software and physical platforms to customers.
This consolidation seeks to address the long-term reliability challenges associated with deploying autonomous vehicles in routine industrial and airport settings.
The development focuses on creating a unified system to manage these complex ground vehicle operations effectively.
This move signals a trend toward comprehensive, integrated solutions in the autonomous vehicle sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, UM1 Evo!".
This segment reports on the development of the UM1 Evo, a biomechanical robotic hand, and its performance evaluation.
The prototype achieved an overall score of six out of ten, emphasizing dexterity over raw strength, with a perfect rating for Degrees of Freedom and a lower rating for strength.
The development involved Didier Vançon over five and a half years, integrating biomechanics, manufacturing, electronics, and software to create the prototype.
The hand weighs one point seven kilograms and incorporates twenty-five electric actuators constructed from custom CNC machined parts.
The project seeks to commercialize the prototype and associated knowledge for fields such as prosthetics and humanoid robotics.
This advancement indicates ongoing progress in the integration of complex biomechanical design into robotic systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, "The Human Layer of the Automated Factory: Keeping People Informed on the Floor"
details the necessity of informing workers regarding changes in automated factory layouts, robot cell locations, and autonomous mobile robot routes to maintain safe and efficient operations.
Automation frequently introduces changes that require more rapid communication than traditional methods such as paper notices.
Digital signage presents a flexible solution for displaying dynamic, high-contrast information, including production targets and safety messages, directly at the point of work.
These displays are designed to integrate with live automation data, such as output counts, to furnish accurate and relevant updates to the workforce.
This system assists the human element of the factory in keeping pace with the swift evolution of machinery.
This development signals an increased integration of real-time data communication into industrial environments across the technology sector.
From Hackaday - Robots, "Robotic Car Charger Locks On With Suction".
This story details the development of a robotic car charger that utilizes suction cups for vehicle attachment and employs remote API calls to manage the charging port.
The key finding is the successful implementation of a physical locking mechanism combined with secure remote control.
The robot employs Mecanum wheels and LiDAR for positioning, alongside an onboard camera utilizing ChARuco patterns for precise alignment.
A gear assembly and suction cups are used to generate the necessary force for connection.
Furthermore, the robot possesses the capability to retract by swiveling its camera to identify wall markers for parking.
This development demonstrates advancements in autonomous physical interaction and secure remote system control within robotics.
Future developments in physical automation and secure IoT integration are anticipated.
From Robotics & Automation News, Honda launches $10,000 challenge to improve human-robot collaboration in factories.
This initiative seeks to foster innovation in optimizing the interaction between human workers and robotic systems within manufacturing environments.

The competition, titled the Automation for Good: The Advanced Manufacturing Challenge, was established in partnership with Base 11 and Freelancer to invite US residents aged eighteen to twenty-six to propose solutions for mitigating workplace hazards using robotics.
Participants were directed to focus their proposals on tasks associated with repetitive lifting, hazardous environments, and ergonomic risks.

The goal of the challenge is to introduce young people to advanced manufacturing careers by emphasizing automation that supports the workforce, offering monetary prizes and mentoring for successful finalists.
This development signals a growing focus on human-centric design within the application of automation technologies.
From Humanoid.guide, Pilatus tests the AEON humanoid for PC-24 airframe inspections, focusing on quality control tasks within manufacturing operations.

The testing involved the integration of the AEON platform, which incorporates sensors, artificial intelligence, precision measurement, and motion control, to autonomously inspect components of a PC-24 business jet in Stans, Switzerland.

The methodology centered on employing the humanoid to perform quality checks on the airframe parts, utilizing its integrated systems to navigate and assess specific areas according to established quality control protocols.
This technology is designed to assist workers by handling repetitive or demanding inspection tasks with greater accuracy.
The deployment of such robotics aims to enhance quality assurance processes and improve worker assistance in industrial settings.
Future plans involve expanding the use of humanoids to advance safety and autonomy in manufacturing environments.
This development signals a progression toward applying advanced robotics in detailed industrial quality control.

From Robotics & Automation News, Comau and Automha showcased integrated food and beverage automation at Cibus Tec 2026, emphasizing the integration of robotics, automated storage, and intralogistics technologies for optimizing the entire value chain.
At the event, Comau presented new food-grade robots and wearable devices engineered for food handling and ergonomic support.
Simultaneously, Automha displayed advanced warehouse technologies, including multi-directional shuttles, designed to enhance storage density and material handling efficiency.
The joint presentation underscored the necessity for manufacturers to establish connections between production processes and automated logistics systems to create a unified automation partner.
This integration seeks to optimize the food and beverage value chain through cohesive technological solutions.
This trend indicates a growing industry focus on holistic system integration within automation and logistics.
From Robotics & Automation News, Luck Stone builds on autonomous hauling success with Caterpillar.

This report details the expansion of autonomous hauling technology across two additional Virginia operations, building upon prior success at Bull Run Quarry where autonomous trucks have managed over three point five million tons.
The collaboration focuses on enhancing safety, ensuring production consistency, and facilitating associate skill development through the application of this technology.
The expansion involves deploying Caterpillar's autonomous hauling solution utilizing Cat 775 trucks at the Boscobel and Bealeton sites.
Collectively, the implementation of Caterpillar autonomous trucks has demonstrated significant achievements in both hauling capacity and safe operational performance.
This development indicates a growing trend in integrating autonomous systems for operational efficiency and workforce upskilling within heavy industry.
From Waymo Blog, "Introducing the Waymo Accessibility Network UK: Co-Designing the Future of Autonomous Mobility".
This announcement details the launch of the Accessibility Network UK, a framework established to ensure autonomous mobility in the United Kingdom is inclusive and tailored to local requirements.
The network facilitates a direct dialogue between Waymo and disability advocates to guide technology deployment.
This initiative provides essential feedback informing the development of features such as vehicle-finding tools, audio cues, and screen reader compatibility.

Specific accessible features discussed include sound alerts, visual identifiers, and customizable in-vehicle options for passengers, actively involving organizations such as the RNIB and Guide Dogs UK in this process.
This effort aims to develop a more accessible autonomous travel experience.
The development of this network indicates a focus on integrating accessibility into the core design of autonomous systems moving forward.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Anigon!".
This report details the introduction of Anigon, an industrial wheeled humanoid developed by Aimbo Robotics for logistics and manufacturing applications.
Anigon stands at 189 centimeters and is equipped with force-controlled arms possessing twenty-eight degrees of freedom, incorporating tactile sensing and RGB depth cameras for object interaction.
The robot utilizes its mobile base and manipulation hardware to perform tasks such as obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly.
It features hot-swappable batteries and safety mechanisms including collision detection and electromagnetic brakes.
Currently, Anigon operates as a prototype with enterprise software integration potential, demonstrating development in navigation and manipulation skills.
This progression indicates continued advancement in embodied AI systems for industrial automation.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, X Hand M1!".
This report details the introduction of the X Hand M1, a rigid robotic hand manufactured by Yuequan Bionics in Beijing, China, designed for industrial applications based on human hand proportions.
The device measures 190 by 90 by 35 millimeters and has a mass of 0.6 kilograms, incorporating five fingers.
Component ratings assigned to the hand indicated moderate degrees of freedom and lower strength, suggesting a requirement for task-specific evaluation.
The product is currently listed as in production with an advertised price of seven thousand US dollars.
This development signals ongoing progress in the creation of functional, anthropomorphic robotic components for advanced industrial deployment.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, FF Nova!".
This report details the introduction of the FF Nova, a compact humanoid robot from Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. demonstrating capabilities in obstacle avoidance and balance recovery.
The FF Nova is priced at two thousand four hundred ninety dollars and is designed for developers, educators, and researchers.
The robot incorporates twenty degrees of freedom and electric servo actuators, along with sensing capabilities including a camera, a Time of Flight sensor, and a two-dimensional LiDAR.
Demonstrations show the robot successfully executing obstacle avoidance and regaining an upright position following a fall, positioning it as an introductory educational platform.
The system supports development through an open software development kit and provides hardware for studying environmental perception and balance recovery.
This development indicates a focus on foundational skills in robotic systems for further exploration.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Star!".
This report details the specifications and current status of Star, a humanoid robot developed for industrial manufacturing.
Star is a 172 centimeter tall, 72 kilogram bipedal humanoid robot featuring seven-axis arms with a dual arm payload capacity of 10 kilograms and thirty-two degrees of freedom.
The robot is capable of walking at a speed of three kilometers per hour and has demonstrated abilities in obstacle avoidance and sorting goods.

Current assessments indicate that the robot's skill score is low, with navigation and manipulation capabilities rated at preliminary levels, positioning Star as an early-stage prototype investigating a humanoid format for factory automation.
This development indicates ongoing exploration into the practical application of humanoid robotics within automated manufacturing environments.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, KAIST!".
This report details the development of a humanoid research prototype by the Dynamic Robot Control and Design Lab, demonstrating capabilities in movement and spatial awareness.

The prototype measures one hundred sixty-five centimeters tall and weighs seventy-five kilograms and exhibits abilities in obstacle avoidance, running one hundred meters, ascending stairs, and performing jumps and landings.
The robot's Humanoid Guide Skill Score is recorded at four out of ten, with navigation rated four out of five and manipulation rated zero out of five, indicating a primary strength in mobility.

The system utilizes internally developed components and reinforcement learning for its control mechanisms, with the prototype having a listed price of one hundred fifty thousand US dollars and being designated for research purposes.
This advancement signals ongoing progress in the integration of complex physical movement into advanced robotics research.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: TC-PEBRAS is hosting a video competition! $250 awards, 3 min videos, due Dec 12, 2026".
This report details an upcoming video competition hosted by TC-PEBRAS focused on robot performance evaluation and benchmarking.
The competition requires participants to create three-minute videos addressing topics such as metrics, test methods, and reproducibility within the fields of robotics and automation.
Submissions are due by December twelfth, two thousand twenty-six, to the specified email address.
Four awards of two hundred fifty dollars will be distributed for submissions demonstrating general scope and for Humanoids twenty twenty-six activities.
The competition officially opens on November fifth, two thousand twenty-six, with the results announced on December seventeenth, two thousand twenty-six.
This initiative serves to enhance public understanding of critical evaluation processes in robotics technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Machinery Positioning Options For Fabrication Facilities: A 2026 Shortlist For Industrial Buyers".
This story outlines the optimal machinery positioning methods for fabrication facilities based on documented requirements.
The most effective positioning method is determined by assessing four documented requirements: clearance, load, movement, and floor condition.
Available options include hydraulic toe jacks, low-profile machinery sliders, wheeled skates, air casters, overhead cranes, and forklifts.
Buyers are advised to evaluate positioning equipment against these four criteria for each move rather than selecting tools based on availability.
Machinery sliders provide a low-profile solution for confined spaces and can accommodate multidirectional maneuvering.
A complete move checklist should incorporate weight, clearance, floor capacity, debris removal, and alignment plans.
This data indicates that facility planning must integrate physical constraints into machinery relocation strategies moving forward.
From aibusinessweekly.net, Axon Invests $1.2B in Skydio, Gets Exclusive Drone Rights.
This report details a significant investment made by Axon into drone maker Skydio, resulting in Axon acquiring a substantial stake in the company.
The agreement, finalized on November 5, 2026, involved Axon investing one point two billion dollars into Skydio, increasing its ownership to thirty-seven percent.
The valuation of Skydio was assessed at five point two billion dollars before the investment.
Axon's payment structure included sixty percent cash and forty percent stock, with a portion of the funding derived from one point one five billion dollars in convertible notes.
Skydio will maintain operational independence, concentrating on autonomous flight development while Axon secures a specific sales channel.
This transaction signals further integration between advanced technology and public safety applications in the technology sector.
From The Robot Report, "How to minimize Wi-Fi roaming interruptions for autonomous mobile robots".
This report details methods for autonomous mobile robots to achieve reliable and fast Wi-Fi roaming by mitigating interruptions caused by traditional network searching.
A dedicated scanning architecture, exemplified by the Synaptics Scan Core, separates network discovery from application traffic through a low-power subsystem.
This separation enables faster roaming decisions and reduces latency and packet loss during transitions between coverage zones.
Implementing this dedicated scanning mechanism allows for continuous network awareness, thereby enhancing the overall performance of mobile robots.
This advancement signifies a path toward more robust and efficient wireless communication for autonomous systems.
From Humanoids Daily, Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch, One Tactile Model for Three Sensor Types.

This story details the release of a tactile model that unifies signals from magnetic, visuotactile, and piezoresistive sensors into shared tactile tokens, demonstrating that integrating these tokens into robot policies significantly increased success rates across various real-robot tasks compared to using raw sensor data.

The research involved training the model on nearly five thousand hours of touch recordings from human operators to create these tactile tokens, which were then integrated into policies for models such as LingBot-VLA and T-Rex, showing substantial performance gains.
Limitations in the study included testing with only two hands and a focus on fingertip contact, alongside the exclusion of capacitive sensor data from the pretraining set.
This work indicates a pathway for more robust tactile perception in robotic systems.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Avatar!".
This report details the development of Avatar, a wheeled humanoid prototype from Honda R&D Co., Ltd. which demonstrates remote physical work capabilities.
The prototype measures one hundred fifty-five centimeters in height and weighs one hundred one kilograms, featuring two arms equipped with five-fingered hands.
The system functions by utilizing tactile feedback and visual cameras to enable remote guidance for tasks such as sorting and assembly.
Operator interaction is managed through a virtual reality headset and gloves, with artificial intelligence assisting in the execution of fine motions.
Honda plans to implement Avatar in fields including medical support, equipment maintenance, and disaster response.
This development indicates ongoing progress in teleoperated robotics and human-robot interaction systems.
And that’s all the circuits for today!
Hope you debugged some interesting insights on agentic systems.
Keep those algorithms humming, and I'll catch you in the next byte!
